subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC derivation key

question: What durable Mattermost interaction signing-secret model should replace the bot-token-derived HMAC before the linked fix can land?
rationale: The code defect is clear, but the replacement changes a credential and callback authorization boundary where persistence, setup discovery, SecretRef handling, upgrade behavior, and fail-closed semantics need maintainer security intent.

options.title: Require Durable Provisioning
options.body: Use a persisted or SecretRef-backed per-account interaction secret with setup/docs/test coverage and prove valid callbacks still work after restart or split sender/verifier execution.

options.title: Accept Explicit Fail-Closed Setup
options.body: Require operators to configure an interaction secret before enabling Mattermost buttons, with clear runtime errors, docs, and tests for the missing-secret path.

options.title: Pause For Replacement
options.body: Keep the issue open and pause the conflicting branch until maintainers choose the credential model, then sponsor a narrow replacement PR.

recommendation.title: Require Durable Provisioning
recommendation.body: Use a persisted or SecretRef-backed per-account interaction secret with setup/docs/test coverage and prove valid callbacks still work after restart or split sender/verifier execution.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed/co-authored the original interaction implementation and later authored the Mattermost callback-reachability change on the same endpoint.
